export ui-component Planning:
    pitch:
        A plain, quick list of the work still to do, as Linear keeps issues:
        stories written ahead of time, each saying how it will be sent, Code,
        Chain, Spec, Ask, or Freeform, gathered into the next sprint and sent
        to the agent in order, all at once.

    description:
        Planning opens in a tab of its own in the body, "Planning", with a
        checklist icon, as a file opens, as the @{Body} says, from the
        ribbon's Planning tab or the palette's "Planning". It is a kanban
        board, filling the body beneath the tab bar, as the @{Body} places
        it, from the tab bar down to the chat input and from the body's left
        edge to its right. Its sections sit side by side as columns, in the
        order work moves, left to right: "Backlog", "Next sprint", "Current
        sprint", and "Done", then "Findings", the last, as research says.
        Each column is headed by its name and count, with its actions, as the
        layout says, and holds its stories as cards, one beneath another. Every
        column is always there, whatever it holds; one with nothing in it
        shows its empty state, as the states say.

    stories:
        A story is one piece of work, written as it will be sent: a title,
        a prompt, and how it will be sent. Each is a story card in its
        column, as the parts say, quiet and dense, as Linear keeps an issue,
        showing all a story shows: a drag grip at its top left; its title
        beside it, the card's one primary thing, in the body's text colour,
        wrapping onto a second line and cut off with an ellipsis only after
        that; and beneath the title, a single muted property row of small
        items: a small mode picker, a pill reading its mode, "Code", "Chain",
        "Spec", "Ask", or "Freeform", in that mode's colour, as the
        @{PromptModes} colours it; its step count and a small icon for
        anything attached, when it has them; and, once it has been sent, its
        status, as a task's is shown, at the row's right. Hovering a card
        shows a menu button at its top right. A story has no Send of its own,
        as the sprint says.

        A column is too narrow to open a story in place, so clicking a card
        never expands it beneath itself or moves the cards below it: it opens
        the story in the side panel, docked at the board's right, as the
        layout places it and the parts draw a panel, headed by the story's
        title. The panel holds all an open story holds: its title, editable
        in place; its prompt, in a
        @{GrowingTextInput} with the chat input's highlighting, completions,
        and slicing, as the @{ChatInput} has, and its attachments beneath;
        its parameters, its mode, model, effort, and Slice, as the chat
        input shows them; its steps, with Add step, as its steps say; and
        its Spec citations, as the spec grounding says. Every change is saved
        as it is made. While its story is open, its card stays highlighted,
        its line in the theme's accent, so which story the panel shows is
        always plain. Only one story is open at a time: clicking another
        card opens that one in the panel instead. Escape, the panel's close
        button, or clicking the open story's card again closes it, and its
        card's highlight with it.

    creating:
        Creating a story is quick, as adding a card is in Trello and adding
        an issue is in Linear: a story is added in the list it belongs in,
        right where it will sit. The Backlog and Next sprint each end with an
        "Add story" line at their foot, beneath their last card, or beneath
        their empty state when they have none. Clicking it opens a composer
        in its place: a blank story card, drawn as the parts draw one, whose
        title is a text box, focused, in the mode last picked for a story,
        with nothing else to fill in. Typing a title and pressing Enter adds
        the story to that list, where the composer was, and opens another
        composer beneath it, so a list can be written down without the
        mouse. Enter with the title empty adds nothing. Escape discards the
        composer, and whatever was typed in it, and the "Add story" line
        comes back; clicking away while its title is empty discards it too,
        and clicking away with a title typed adds the story, as Enter does,
        but opens no other composer. A story added this way is not opened in
        the side panel; its card is there to be clicked, as the stories say,
        once more than its title is wanted.

        Hovering the Backlog's or Next sprint's heading shows a labelled
        "+ Add" button in it, as the layout places it, which opens the
        composer at the top of that list, above its first card, so a story
        can go first without being dragged there; Enter adds it there and
        opens the next composer beneath it, so stories written one after
        another keep the order they were written in. Ctrl+N (Cmd+N on macOS)
        while Planning has focus opens the composer at the foot of the list
        that has focus, the Backlog or Next sprint, as the keyboard says, and
        at the foot of Next sprint when neither has it. Only one composer is
        open at a time: opening another discards an empty one and adds one
        with a title, as clicking away does. Current sprint, Done, and
        Findings have no "Add story" line, no "+ Add", and no composer, and
        Ctrl+N never adds a story to them.

        A story goes into the list it was added to, then: the Backlog or
        Next sprint, whichever composer it was written in. A duplicate goes
        into its original's list, just beneath it, and a story added from an
        Ask answer's card with "Add to sprint" goes into Next sprint, at its
        end. An accepted proposal for a new story, from drafting, research,
        or an Ask answer's proposal card, still goes into the Backlog, at its
        end, as the proposal cards say, and reaches a sprint only once it is
        moved to Next sprint. A story can always be moved between the two
        afterwards, as the sprint says. Adding a story never starts a sprint
        by itself, except where Start automatically starts one when a story
        is added to an empty Next sprint, as auto start says; a story added
        to the Backlog never starts one. A title with no prompt sends its
        title as its prompt.

        A story can also be prompted into existence: "Draft stories", a
        button beside the Backlog's heading, opens a small box to say what is
        wanted, in a sentence or a paragraph, and asks the harness, in a run
        of its own with no session, with the planning prompt of the
        @{BakedSystemPrompts}, to break it into stories, each with a title, a
        prompt, and the mode that fits it. They come back as proposals, as
        the drafting and proposals say, each to be accepted, edited, or
        rejected, and none reaches the plan until it is accepted. An Ask
        answer's prompt cards also offer "Add to sprint", which adds the
        card's prompt as a story in its mode to Next sprint.

    sprint:
        Stories move between the Backlog and Next sprint by dragging, as the
        @{DragReorderBehaviour} says, a card dragged by its grip from one
        column into a gap in the other as within either, the gap opened in
        the column the pointer is over, as motion says; an empty one takes a
        drop at its top. Dragged near the board's left or right edge, the
        board scrolls sideways, and near a column's top or bottom, that
        column scrolls, as dragging says. Only the Backlog and Next sprint
        take drops: Current sprint and Done open no gap, a story
        dropped on them stays where it was, and their cards can't be picked
        up, nor can a finding. Stories move too from a card's menu, "Move to
        next sprint" or "Move to backlog". Their order within Next sprint is
        the order they will be sent. A card's menu also has "Duplicate" and
        "Delete".

        "Send sprint", a primary button at the right of Next sprint's
        heading, enabled while it holds a story, sends every story in it, in
        order, as though each had been written in the chat input on its
        mode's tab and sent, one after another, as the @{PromptSending} says:
        each task queues in its lane behind the one before it, in the order
        of the sprint, and each question runs at once. The stories go into
        the queue as one block, so nothing sent later comes between them,
        and the queue's auto-send carries them on as ever, as the
        @{QueueList} says.

        Each story starts a conversation of its own, as though New
        conversation had been pressed just before it, and so does each later
        step of a story's chain: a story never carries on the conversation of
        the story before it, nor of anything its lane ran before the sprint.
        New conversation, pressed before the sprint was sent, is left for the
        next prompt written in the chat input.

        A story can't be sent on its own. The only way a story reaches work
        is through the sprint: a story in the Backlog waits until it is
        moved into Next sprint and the sprint is sent, and a story in Next
        sprint goes when the sprint does. Nothing in Planning, its cards,
        their menus, the open story, the keyboard, the palette, or the
        ribbon, sends a single story, and nothing elsewhere sends a story by
        any other route: a story can't be dragged or copied into the chat
        input or the queue to be sent from there, and its menu has no "Send"
        or "Edit in chat input". The chat input's own prompts are not
        stories and are sent as ever; once a prompt is a story, the sprint is
        its only way to work. To send one story at once, it is the only story in
        Next sprint when Send sprint is pressed. A story that failed or was
        cancelled is sent again the same way, with the next sprint.

        Sending the sprint moves its stories into the "Current sprint"
        column, to the right of Next sprint, so Next sprint is empty again
        and stories added meanwhile go there, to be the sprint after. Current
        sprint and Done are columns of the board whatever they hold, never
        appearing, disappearing, or collapsing; while no sprint is under way
        Current sprint is empty and shows its empty state, as Done does
        before anything is done. A story in Current sprint keeps its place,
        its card showing its task's status as it queues, runs, and ends, and clicking
        it opens its task in the Tasks tab; it can't be moved or edited
        there. Once every story of Current sprint has ended, its column's
        heading offers "Close sprint", which moves the stories that are done
        into the Done column, their cards muted, and those that
        failed, were cancelled, or stopped to the start of Next sprint, in
        their order, to be sent again. While a sprint is current, Send sprint
        is disabled, its tooltip saying a sprint is already under way.

        Send sprint only ever moves into Current sprint the stories it
        actually sent. A story with nothing to send, its title and its prompt
        both empty, is skipped: it stays in Next sprint, where it was, and
        Send sprint's result says, muted, how many it skipped and why, as "1
        empty story left in Next sprint". A sprint where every story is
        empty sends nothing and makes no Current sprint.

        Once a sprint is done, it can always be closed. Every story of
        Current sprint counts as ended once its task has ended, done,
        failed, cancelled, or stopped, or once its task can no longer be
        found, as when its record was deleted, it was never recorded, or the
        application quit before it was. A story whose task is missing is
        never shown as Queued, or as anything still to come: its card reads
        "Task missing", muted, in the theme's warning colour, its tooltip
        saying its task can't be found, and it counts as ended and not Done.
        A story still waiting in its lane's queue, or held for review, as
        the paused section says, is still to come and hasn't ended. So Close
        sprint shows as soon as no story of Current sprint is building,
        compiling, running, paused, queued, or held, and never waits on a
        task that can't arrive.

        Close sprint treats a story whose task is missing as it treats one
        that failed or was cancelled: it goes back to the start of Next
        sprint, with the others sent again, in their order, never into Done.
        Closing saves the sections, Done, Next sprint, the Backlog, and
        the emptied Current sprint, to `order.json` straight away, as the
        @{ProjectData} says, and Current sprint's state is worked out afresh
        from the stories' tasks whenever the plan is read, so a sprint that
        finished, or whose tasks went missing, before a reload or a restart
        can still be closed after it, as before.

    motion:
        Dragging a card on the board feels as it does in Trello, and the
        board opens the gap, as the @{DragReorderBehaviour} lets its user do,
        in place of the accent line alone. Only the board's cards move this
        way; steps in an open story, and every other list, are dragged as
        the @{DragReorderBehaviour} says, with its line.

        A card picked up by its grip lifts off the board as a full-size copy
        of itself, the same width and height, drawn as the parts draw a
        story card, tilted a few degrees, about 3, on the theme's overlay
        surface with its edge border and the soft shadow the @{Theme}'s
        elevation gives floating surfaces, the one shadow on the board. It
        follows the pointer, held where it was grabbed, and never takes the
        mouse. The card's own place in its column becomes the gap it left,
        empty, the card's height, so the column doesn't jump as it lifts.

        Where the card would land, the cards slide apart to open a
        placeholder the dragged card's height, 8 pixels from the cards
        either side, as the cards are spaced: a box the card's size on the
        theme's well surface, with its corners rounded 6 pixels as a card's
        are, and no border, so it reads as an empty slot. The gap is chosen
        as the @{DragReorderBehaviour} chooses it, among the cards of the
        column the pointer is over, and only one is open at a time: as the
        pointer moves into another gap, or another column, the gap it left
        closes as the new one opens, and the gap the card came from closes
        once the pointer leaves its column, opening again if it comes back.
        A column that takes no drops opens no gap, and its cards never move
        while a card is dragged over it.

        Nothing waits on motion while the user is waiting on it. The gap the
        card would drop into is updated at once, the moment the pointer
        crosses the middle of a card, exactly as the
        @{DragReorderBehaviour} says, and a drop always goes where the gap
        was chosen, even while the cards are still sliding toward it; only
        the sliding of the cards around it is animated, quickly, as below.

        Dropped over an open gap, the copy settles into it: it straightens,
        its shadow fades, and it moves from where it was released into the
        placeholder, which it then is, the story saved in its new place at
        the moment of the drop, as every change to the plan is. Dropped
        anywhere else, or where it began, it settles back into the gap it
        came from the same way, and nothing changes. Escape while dragging
        cancels it, settling the card back where it was.

        A card moved any other way animates to its new place, in Linear's
        style: a quick motion of about 150 milliseconds, eased out, sliding
        from where it was to where it now is, the cards it passes or leaves
        sliding to close and open the room it takes, never fading or
        bouncing. That covers every move the sprint describes: "Move to next
        sprint" and "Move to backlog" from a card's menu, Alt+Up, Alt+Down,
        Alt+Left, and Alt+Right, Ctrl+Enter, Send sprint moving its stories
        into Current sprint, and Close sprint moving them into Done and back
        to the start of Next sprint. A card added, as by a composer or
        Duplicate, slides the cards below it down to make room, and a card
        deleted slides them up to close it, in the same motion. The board
        scrolls sideways, and a column up or down, to keep a moved card that
        has focus in view, as the keyboard says. Focus goes with the card
        at once, not when its motion ends, and the plan is saved at once.

        The side panel slides in from the board's right as it opens, in the
        same quick motion, the board narrowing alongside it, and slides back
        out to the right as it closes, the board widening as it goes;
        replacing what it holds with another story, drafting, or research
        changes its content in place, with no slide. Its content, and focus
        in it, are there as soon as it starts to open.

        Every motion here takes about 150 milliseconds, never longer, and a
        move made while another is still under way starts from wherever the
        card is then, never queued behind it.

    autoStart:
        Next sprint can start on its own: a "Start automatically" switch on
        Next sprint's heading, beside Send sprint, its tooltip saying the
        next sprint starts as soon as the current one is done. It starts
        off, and is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, so it is kept
        across reloads and restarts.

        While it is on, once every story of Current sprint has ended Done,
        the current sprint closes by itself, as Close sprint closes it, and
        Next sprint, if it holds a story, is sent at once, as Send sprint
        sends it, with nobody having to start it; and while no sprint is
        current, a story added to an empty Next sprint starts it the same
        way. A sprint that ended with a story failed, cancelled, stopped, or with its task missing,
        never starts the next by itself: it waits, Close sprint offered as
        ever, and the switch's row says, in the theme's warning colour, why
        the next didn't start. Nor does the next start while planning is
        paused, as the paused section says: it starts once the pause is
        ended by Resume, or Approve, if the switch is still on. An empty Next
        sprint starts nothing.

        Each time a sprint starts by itself, a passive notification says
        so, "Next sprint started: 4 stories", with a link that opens
        Planning, and the debug log records it. Turning the switch off
        never stops a sprint already sent; it only keeps the next from
        starting by itself. Turning it on while no sprint is current and
        Next sprint holds a story starts Next sprint at once, as adding a
        story to it would, unless planning is paused.

        The switch works while Planning isn't open, from the plan as saved,
        whichever tab is shown. When the project is opened, or the
        application starts, with the switch on, no sprint current, and Next
        sprint holding a story, it doesn't start by itself; the switch's row
        says, muted, "Waiting to start", with a "Start now" button, so a
        sprint never begins unseen as the application opens. A current
        sprint whose stories were cut off when the application quit, as
        every run is, ended them, and never starts the next by itself.

        While the switch is on, Next sprint's heading shows "Auto" beside
        its count, in the theme's accent, and the ribbon's Send Sprint
        button's tooltip says the next sprint starts automatically.

    saving:
        The stories, their order, and which section each is in are saved
        with the project's data, as the @{ProjectData} says, in
        `.suspense/planning/`, a file per story, holding its hidden anchor
        as a queued prompt's is, and an `order.json` listing the sections and
        their stories, so the plan is kept with the project and comes back
        as it was left. A story's steps are saved in its own file, in their
        order, as its steps say, never apart from it.

    steps:
        A story can have steps: one or more further prompts, each a piece of
        the story done after the one before, as a chain's steps are. Each
        step has a prompt, a mode of its own, Code or Spec, starting as the
        story's, and a model and effort, starting as the story's, and may
        have attachments. A story with no steps is just its own prompt, as
        before; its prompt is always its first step.

        An open story lists its steps beneath its prompt, in order, each a
        row numbered from 2, the story's own prompt being 1, with its mode
        pill and the first line of its prompt, opening in place to edit, as
        a story does. "Add step", beneath the last, adds one at the end,
        open and focused; several can be added one after another, Enter in
        an empty step's prompt adding none. Steps are reordered by dragging,
        as the @{DragReorderBehaviour} says, or Alt+Up and Alt+Down, and each
        has a remove button in its row and in its menu. The story's own
        prompt stays first and can't be moved among them.

        A step belongs to its story and to nothing else. It is saved in the
        story's file, in a `steps` list of the story's hidden anchor, in its
        order, and saved as every change to the plan is, straight away; a
        story duplicated copies its steps, and one deleted deletes them. Its
        order is kept wherever the story goes, between sections, into a
        sprint, and back from Done.

        Wherever the story is shown, its steps are too: its card in Planning
        shows how many beneath its title, muted, as "3 steps", with the list in
        its tooltip; the open story lists them as above; a proposal to add
        to it shows them, so what it would add to can be seen; and once it
        is sent, it is sent as a chain, its prompt first and each step after
        it in order, each step sent only once the one before it finishes, as
        the @{PromptEditor}'s chained tasks are, so the Tasks tab shows the
        story as one chain with its steps beneath it. A story sent can't be
        given more steps; its steps, sent or still to come, read as they
        were sent. In Current sprint, a story with steps lists its steps on
        its card, beneath its title, a line for each step, in order, each
        with its number, the first line of its prompt cut off with an
        ellipsis, and its own status, as a running chain's are in the Tasks
        tab; in Done, and
        in a finding started from the story, its steps are listed the same
        way, collapsed to its step count until it is expanded. The same steps,
        in the same order, are what every place shows, since every place
        reads them from the story's own file.

        A step is only ever added to a story that exists. Adding one to a
        story that doesn't, as one deleted while a proposal naming it waited,
        or by another window, or whose file was removed from
        `.suspense/planning/` meanwhile, changes nothing: no story is made
        for it, no other story is given it, and nothing is saved. It says so
        in plain words where it was asked for, as "That story no longer
        exists, so the step wasn't added", in the theme's error colour, as
        the states say, with what was to be added kept, so it can be added
        to another story or as a new one. A step added to a story already
        sent is refused the same way, saying the story has been sent.

    layout:
        Everything in Planning is laid out on one rhythm, so the board scans
        at a glance. The board fills the body beneath the tab bar, with 24
        pixels of padding at its top, sides, and foot. Its columns are all
        the same fixed width, 320 pixels, 16 pixels apart, each as tall as
        the board, set side by side from its left edge in the order work
        moves, Backlog, Next sprint, Current sprint, Done, and Findings, the
        last. Each column is a list, as Trello draws one: a container of its
        own, as the parts draw a list, on the theme's recessed surface, one
        step from the base the board is on, its corners rounded 8 pixels,
        with its heading and its cards inside it; its surface and the gaps
        between columns set it apart, and it has no border.

        Each column's heading reads as Linear heads a group: a row 32 pixels
        tall at the list's top, holding, from its left, the column's status
        icon, 14 pixels, as the parts give it; its name in small semibold
        text, in the theme's primary text colour; its count beside it, muted;
        and its actions at its right, each a labelled button, never an icon
        alone, as the sections give them: "Draft stories" and "Research" on
        the Backlog; "Send sprint" and "Start automatically" on Next sprint;
        "Close sprint" on Current sprint, once its sprint can close. A
        heading with more actions than fit its width wraps them onto a second
        line beneath its name rather than cutting any off. On the Backlog and
        Next sprint, hovering the heading, or focus anywhere in it, shows
        "+ Add" just after its count, a small ghost button with a plus icon
        and its label, never the icon alone, its tooltip saying it adds a
        story at the top of the list; it takes its room in the heading
        whether shown or not, so the heading's actions never shift as it
        appears, and the other columns' headings have none. 8 pixels beneath
        the heading come its cards, one beneath another, 8 pixels apart, each
        the list's full inner width.

        At the foot of the Backlog and of Next sprint, 8 pixels beneath its
        last card, or beneath its empty state, is its "Add story" line: a
        row 32 pixels tall, the list's full inner width, with a plus icon and
        the label "Add story" in small muted text, its corners rounded 6
        pixels, and no border; hovered, it takes the theme's hover surface
        and its text the theme's primary text colour. It scrolls with the
        cards, after the last of them. Its composer, as creating says, is
        drawn where it was clicked, at the foot in the line's place, or at
        the top, above the first card, from "+ Add": a story card, as the
        parts draw one, its title a text box in the card's title text, with
        the focus ring around the card, and beneath it, muted, "Enter to add,
        Escape to cancel"; the cards below it move down to make room, and the
        list scrolls to keep it in view. Current sprint, Done, and Findings
        have no "Add story" line.

        Each column scrolls up and down on its own, its heading staying at
        its top while its cards scroll beneath it, inside the list's rounded
        corners, with the @{Scrollbar} shown along the list's right, inside
        it, while it holds more than fits. The board
        scrolls sideways when its columns are wider than the tab, with the
        @{Scrollbar} along its foot; while they fit, it doesn't scroll. Every
        card's state reads the same way, as below, and every label is the
        same small text, muted where it is secondary.

        The side panel is the one place anything opens: an open story, Draft
        stories, and Research, never beneath a heading or a card, and never
        in a popup or over the board. A composer is not an opened story but
        a card being written, and is the one thing drawn in a list, where its
        story will sit. It is docked at the right of Planning's
        tab, 400 pixels wide, as tall as the tab, from the tab bar down to the
        chat input, a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour along its left
        edge, and it scrolls up and down on its own, its heading staying at
        its top, with the @{Scrollbar} along its right while it holds more
        than fits. Only one thing is in it at a time: opening a story,
        drafting, or research replaces whatever it held, and closing it
        leaves nothing there. While it is open the board narrows to the space
        left of it, its columns keeping their width and scrolling sideways
        as ever when they no longer fit; the panel never covers the board,
        and the board never covers it. Closed, it takes no space and the
        board fills the tab again. It slides in and out at the right, as
        motion says.

        While paused, the pause bar runs across the top of the whole board,
        above every column, as the paused section says, beside the side
        panel when it is open, never over it. Each column is
        headed as above, so nothing sits outside the rhythm, and an open
        story, a drafting or research panel, and the citations and steps
        inside a story all use the same five parts, below.

    parts:
        Everything in Planning is built from five parts, each always drawn
        the same way, in the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in
        both dark and light mode:

        \\
        - A list: one per column, as the layout places it, 320 pixels wide and as tall as the board, on the theme's recessed surface, one step from the base, with no border, its corners rounded 8 pixels, 8 pixels of padding; its heading row at its top, as the layout says, then its cards, or its empty state centred beneath its heading; its heading's status icon one per column, each always the same: the Backlog a dashed circle in the theme's tertiary text colour; Next sprint an empty circle in the theme's secondary text colour; Current sprint a half-filled circle in the theme's accent; Done a filled circle with a check in the theme's success colour; and Findings a magnifying glass in the theme's secondary text colour; each only repeating the column's name, never standing for it
        - A story card: a box the full inner width of its list, on the theme's raised surface, with a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour, corners rounded 6 pixels, 8 pixels of padding above and below and 10 at its sides, 8 pixels from the next; a top line with its drag grip, 16 pixels, in the theme's tertiary text colour, at its left, its title beside it, the card's primary text, in up to two lines, cut off with an ellipsis after the second, and its menu button at its right on hover and always while it is focused; beneath the title, 4 pixels below it, a single property row, 20 pixels tall, in small muted text, of small items 8 pixels apart: its mode pill, in its mode's colour, as the PromptModes colours it, its step count, its attachment icon, each when it has them, and its status and time, right-aligned, once it has been sent; and, in Current sprint, its steps' lines beneath, as its steps say; used for every story, in every column, muted in Done. Its states are three distinct steps, as the Theme's hierarchy orders them: hovering raises it one surface step, to the theme's hover surface; the open story keeps a 3 pixel line in the theme's accent along its left edge, as the stories say, whether or not it is hovered; a selected card, as the selection below says, takes the theme's selected surface in place of its raised one, hovered or not; and focus shows the theme's focus ring, in the accent, 2 pixels around it, over any of them, so a hover is always quieter than a selection, and a selection than focus, as the Theme orders them, and the open story's line, an edge rather than a surface, reads apart from both, a card being open, selected, and focused at once without any of the three hiding another
        - A row: 36 pixels tall, for steps in an open story and for findings; its secondary text muted and cut off with an ellipsis, its buttons small ghost buttons with labels, shown at its right on hover and always while it is focused
        - A panel: the side panel, docked at the board's right, full height, as the layout places it, on the theme's raised surface, its corners square, 12 pixels of padding, a heading row of 32 pixels with its name, as "Draft stories", "Research", or the story's title, and its close button, its content beneath, and its actions in a footer row, right-aligned, the primary action last; used for an open story, drafting, and research
        - A card: a box inside a panel, on the theme's base surface, with a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour, corners rounded 4 pixels, 12 pixels of padding, 8 pixels from the next; a label row at its top, its content, and a footer row of labelled buttons; used for proposals and for each finding's summary
        \\

        Labels are words, never icons alone: every button reads what it
        does, "Accept", "Send sprint", "Start automatically", and an icon
        beside a label only repeats it. Each heading's count is a plain
        number, muted, and each status a coloured label, as the states say.
        The pause bar is a row across the whole board's top, above its
        columns, 40 pixels tall, its text and buttons on one line, the same
        height whatever it says.

        Stories are selected as Linear selects issues, to be acted on
        together. Only a story in the Backlog or Next sprint can be selected,
        the two lists that take moves, as the sprint says; a card in Current
        sprint or Done, and a finding, never is. Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on
        macOS) on a card toggles it alone in or out of the selection, the
        rest kept; Shift+click selects the range within its column from the
        card last clicked or toggled there to the clicked one, inclusive,
        added to the selection, or the clicked card alone when nothing in
        that column was clicked or toggled yet; and X toggles one from the
        keyboard, as the keyboard says. A selection can hold stories from
        both lists at once. A plain click opens the story in the side panel
        as ever, and leaves the selection as it is. Selected cards show the
        theme's selected surface, as the story card above says, distinct
        from focus and from the open story's line. The selection is the
        board's own, never saved with the plan: a selected story leaves it
        when it is deleted or leaves the Backlog and Next sprint, as when the
        sprint it is in is sent.

        While any card is selected, the bulk bar runs across the board's
        foot, beneath its columns, beside the side panel when it is open,
        never over it nor over the board: a row 40 pixels tall, on the
        theme's raised surface with a 1 pixel line in the theme's line
        colour along its top, the columns shortening to make room as it
        slides up in motion's quick motion, and lengthening again as it
        slides away once nothing is selected. At its left it names how many
        are selected, as "3 selected"; at its right, labelled buttons, never
        icons alone, in this order: "Move to next sprint", which moves the
        selected stories in the Backlog to the end of Next sprint; "Move to
        backlog", which moves those in Next sprint to the end of the
        Backlog; "Change mode", which opens a mode picker above it, the one
        a card's pill opens, setting the mode of every selected story to the
        one picked, their steps keeping their own; "Duplicate", which
        duplicates each, every copy just beneath its original, as a card's
        menu does; "Delete", which deletes them all after one confirmation
        naming how many, as "Delete 3 stories?"; and "Clear", which empties
        the selection. Every move keeps the stories' order, as the selection
        orders them, the Backlog's first, top to bottom, then Next sprint's,
        and animates as motion says; a move button is disabled, its tooltip
        saying why, while none of the selection is in the list it moves
        from. Moved stories stay selected, duplicates are not selected, and
        the originals stay so. The bar has no Send and sends nothing: a
        story still reaches work only through the sprint, as the sprint
        says.

        Dragging a selected card by its grip carries the whole selection,
        in its order: the other selected cards leave their places as it
        lifts, their columns closing up, and the lifted copy is the grabbed
        card, as motion draws it, with the cards it carries stacked a few
        pixels behind it and their count beside its title. The gap opens as
        tall as the cards together, 8 pixels apart, and dropped there they
        settle into it in their order, all in that list, saved at once;
        dropped anywhere else, or cancelled with Escape, they all settle
        back where they were. Dragging a card that isn't selected moves it
        alone and leaves the selection as it is.

        Right-clicking a card opens its menu at the pointer, the same menu
        its hover button opens, with the same items, acting on that card
        alone, in place of the browser's own; it closes as that menu does,
        Escape among the ways.

    states:
        Each part of Planning has the same few states, shown the same way
        wherever they come up, so a state is never guessed from what is
        missing.

        \\
        - Empty: a single muted line, centred in the column beneath its heading, saying what is missing and what to do, as "Nothing planned. Drag stories here, or press Ctrl+N.", with no illustration
        - Loading: a spinner and a short muted label of what is happening, as "Drafting stories…", in the place the result will appear, never a blank space
        - Paused: a story whose task is paused shows "Paused" as its status, in the theme's warning colour, with a small pause icon, and a "Resume" button on its card, as the PromptSending says of pausing; a sprint with any story paused says so in its heading, as "1 paused", in the same colour
        - Error: a line in the theme's error colour, saying what went wrong in plain words, with what the harness or the application reported beneath it collapsed under "Details", and a "Try again" button where trying again can help
        \\

        A story's status on its card is the same coloured label a task has,
        as the @{MessageList}'s status says, Queued, Running with its spinner
        and time, Done, Failed, Cancelled, Paused, or, where its task can't be found, Task missing, as the sprint says, and a story not yet
        sent shows nothing there, so its absence means "not sent".

        Each part shows each state that can come up for it, worded for it:

        \\
        - Story list: empty, "Nothing planned. Press Ctrl+N to add a story." in Next sprint, "Nothing waiting." in the Backlog, "No sprint under way. Send sprint to start one." in Current sprint, and "Nothing done yet." in Done; loading, while the plan is read on opening, a few skeleton cards in each column, never an empty column; error, when the plan can't be read or saved, saying which file and why, with "Try again"
        - Research and its findings: loading, the live line of what it is reading with its spinner; empty, "No findings yet." in Findings; error, the run's failure with "Try again", which keeps the question in its box; a finding that ended early, as stopped, marked "Incomplete", muted, in its row
        - Pause: the pause bar, in the theme's warning colour, as the paused section says, and the sprint's Send buttons disabled with their tooltips saying why; a sprint that can't start for a failed story says so in its heading, in the same colour
        - Proposals: loading, the drafting line and spinner; empty, "No stories proposed." with "Draft again"; error, the run's failure with "Try again"; a proposal with no spec cited, in the warning colour with "Draft again", as the spec grounding says
        \\

    drafting:
        Drafting stories shows its work in one place, the side panel, docked
        at the board's right, as the layout places it, replacing whatever it
        held, never in a popup that hides the list. It has
        the request box at its top, labelled "Describe what you want", and
        beneath it, while the run goes, its research: a muted line of what
        the harness is doing, as "Reading the spec…", with its spinner,
        updating as it goes, and a "Stop" button. Once it ends, the panel
        lists its proposals, as below, then "Accept all" and "Reject all"
        buttons along the panel's foot, and closes itself once none is left
        to decide. A run that fails shows its error, as the states say, and
        leaves the request in its box to try again; one that proposes nothing
        says so, as an empty state. Proposals are kept until each is decided,
        so closing Planning and coming back finds them as they were.

        Drafting can also be started from an open story, with "Ask agent"
        in its card's menu or the open story's footer: the request box then
        reads "What does this story need?", the run is told the story's
        title and prompt, and the drafting panel takes the open story's place
        in the side panel, the story's card staying highlighted while the
        draft is about it.

        The request is sent with the panel's "Draft" button, its primary
        action, or by pressing Enter in the request box, whichever label it
        reads; Ctrl+Enter there starts it too, and the button's tooltip
        gives Enter as its shortcut. Shift+Enter adds a new line in the box
        and sends nothing. A request that is empty, or only spaces and new
        lines, starts nothing, and the button is disabled while it is. While
        a run is going, Enter starts no second one, and the button is
        disabled. Enter in the request box only ever sends the request: the
        list's Enter, opening or closing the focused story, never fires
        while focus is in the box.

    proposals:
        The agent never writes the plan itself. Its run is a Question run,
        as the @{Sandbox} says, able to read the project and change nothing,
        and Suspense data is never granted to it, so it can't touch
        `.suspense/planning/`; it only proposes, and nothing it proposes
        reaches the plan until the user accepts it.

        Each proposal is one concrete task, with a title, a prompt, and the
        mode that fits it, and says where it should go: either "New story",
        to become a story of its own, or "Add to" a story, naming an existing
        story the run was shown, the open story first, to be added to it. The
        planning prompt of the @{BakedSystemPrompts} asks for each proposal
        as a fenced block whose info string is `suspense-story`, holding its
        title, its mode, its target, `new` or the story's id, its `spec`
        list of citations into the Piton source, as the spec grounding says,
        and its prompt, so the application reads it whatever else the reply
        says. The planning prompt explains the form with an example, as:

        \\\
        ```suspense-story
        title: Close a finished sprint
        mode: chain
        target: new
        spec:
        - spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint: when Close sprint shows
        - No match: archiving a closed sprint
        prompt:
        Close sprint is offered once every story of the current sprint has
        ended, as spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint says.
        ```
        \\\

        A
        block that names a story that no longer exists is shown as "New
        story", with a muted note saying so.

    specGrounding:
        A drafted story is grounded in the project's spec, never written
        from the request alone. Before proposing, the drafter searches the
        spec for what each story touches: the requirements and behaviours it
        changes or relies on, the names it uses, as a feature, a component,
        or a property, and the sections they are in. It reads the spec as
        every run does, from its compiled reference or from what `piton
        slice` prints, never from the Piton source, as the
        @{ModeSystemPrompts} says, and the planning prompt of the
        @{BakedSystemPrompts} tells it to.

        Each proposal cites what it found, specifically: its `suspense-story`
        block holds a `spec` list, one entry per element, each a link to the
        element in the spec's Piton source, under the spec location, never
        to the compiled reference: the .pi file, relative to the project
        directory, then `#` and the element it names, an anchor or a
        property on one, in the form `piton slice` takes, as
        `spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint`, with a short line of
        what in it the story touches. The story's prompt names those
        elements and links to them in the same form. Only elements the
        drafter found are cited, and where they point is the only thing
        that is Piton source: the drafter still learns what the spec says
        only from the compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints,
        never by reading the Piton source, as the @{ModeSystemPrompts} says,
        and works out each element's source from what `piton slice` prints
        for it, which names the file each declaration is in.

        The application checks each link against the Piton source when the
        proposal arrives: the file has to exist under the spec location, and
        has to define the named element, the anchor declared in it and, for
        a property, that property on it, as `piton slice` would find it. A
        link that fails either check is dropped, with a muted note on the
        card saying which link it dropped and why, "no such file" or "the
        file doesn't define Planning.sprint". Each citation, on the proposal
        card and in an accepted story's "Spec" list, opens that place in the
        Piton source, the file in the editor at the element's declaration,
        as the @{OpenFile} opens a file.

        Where no spec element matches part of a story, as a request for
        something the spec doesn't describe yet, the story says so instead
        of inventing one: its `spec` list holds an entry reading "No match",
        with what was looked for, and its prompt says plainly that the spec
        has nothing on it yet, so the change is new. A proposal with no
        element at all, and no "No match", isn't shown as a story: its card
        says the drafter cited no spec, in the theme's warning colour, with
        "Draft again", which runs the draft for that story once more.

        The citations are shown on the proposal's card, beneath its prompt,
        as a short list, each element's name, as `Planning.sprint`, and its
        file, muted, as a link that opens that place in the Piton source, a
        "No match" entry muted with a small marker, and are kept with the
        story once it is accepted, listed in the open story beneath its
        steps as "Spec", and shown in its card's tooltip. They can be edited
        with the story, removed, or added to by hand: "Add citation" opens a
        picker of the spec's elements, its anchors and their properties,
        found from the Piton source and searched by name, never from the
        compiled reference, and adds the one picked in the same form,
        checked as a proposal's are.

        Each citation says what kind of element it is, "Requirement",
        "Behaviour", "Name", or "Section", shown as a small muted label
        before it, and quotes the few words of the spec it rests on, so what
        the story relies on can be checked at a glance. Grounding holds for
        every proposal, however it came: from Draft stories, from research
        that ends with proposals, and from an Ask answer's `suspense-story`
        block, each checked and flagged the same way when it arrives.

    proposalCards:
        Each proposal is a card in the panel, in the order given: a label at
        its top, "New story" in the theme's accent, or, for an addition,
        "Add to this story" where it targets the story the research or draft
        was started from, and "Add to" and the story's title otherwise, in
        the story's own mode's colour, so where it will go is always read
        before anything else on the card; its title,
        its mode pill, and its prompt beneath, clipped at four lines with
        "Read more"; and three buttons along its foot, "Accept", "Edit", and
        "Reject", reachable by Tab and labelled for a screen reader. Edit
        opens the card's title, prompt, mode, and target in place, the target
        a menu of "New story" and each story, to be changed before it is
        accepted; editing doesn't accept it. Reject removes the card, with a
        short "Undo" in its place for a few seconds.

        Accept records it in the plan straight away, saved as any change to
        the plan is: a new story goes into the Backlog, at its end, in its
        mode, marked "From agent" with a small sparkle beside its title until
        it is first opened, its spec citations kept with it, whether it was
        accepted on its own card or with "Accept all", and whether it came
        from drafting, research, or an Ask answer. Accepting never adds
        anything to Next sprint, so it never starts a sprint, however Start
        automatically is set; an accepted story reaches a sprint only once it
        is moved to Next sprint, as the sprint says; an addition is added to the named story as a new
        step at its end, as its steps say, its attachments with it, and the
        story is marked "Updated by agent" until it is next opened, the new
        step shown highlighted the first time it is; where the story no
        longer exists by then, the step isn't added, as the steps say, and
        the card stays, its target changed to "New story", to be accepted
        again. A story already sent can't be added to: its
        proposals offer only "New story". Each card, once decided, goes from
        the panel, and an accepted one leaves a one-line muted note in its
        place, "Added to Backlog" or "Added to <story>", with a link that
        opens the story where it is, in the Backlog or its section.

        Ask answers can propose the same way: a `suspense-story` block in an
        answer is shown as a proposal card, with the same Accept, Edit, and
        Reject, its accepting recording it in the plan as above, so a story
        can come out of a conversation without anything written silently.

    research:
        The agent can be asked to research a topic before anything is
        planned or built: "Research", a button beside "Draft stories" on the
        Backlog's heading, and "Research" in an open story's menu, open a
        box labelled "What should be looked into?". Research runs as a
        read-only investigation, a Question run, as the @{Sandbox} says, which
        can read the project and the web and change nothing, given the
        research prompt of the @{BakedSystemPrompts}, which asks for findings,
        not changes: what was found, where, with links to the files and
        lines it read, what it is unsure of, and what it would suggest, and
        it may end with proposals, as the proposals say. Its box and its run
        are shown in the side panel, replacing whatever it held, as
        drafting's are, its live line of what it is reading, a Stop button,
        and its spinner, and its proposals in the same cards with the same
        buttons as drafting's, with Accept all and Reject all at its foot.

        Its findings are a document of their own, "Research: <topic>",
        rendered as markdown with its links clickable, shown in the Findings
        column, the board's last, after Done, newest first, each a row with
        its topic,
        when it ran, and its state, and opening in a body tab of its own to
        read whole. Findings started from a story are also listed in that
        story, beneath its steps. They are saved with the plan, in
        `.suspense/planning/research/`, a markdown file each, so they can be
        read again later, and can be deleted from their row's menu.

    paused:
        Once research ends, however it ended, planning is paused. While it
        is paused nothing is implemented: Send sprint, the
        ribbon's Send Sprint, and the sprint's Ctrl+Shift+Enter are disabled,
        their tooltips saying planning is paused for review, and no proposal
        from the research is added to the plan by itself. Stories can still
        be written, edited, ordered, and moved, and proposals still accepted
        or rejected one by one, since those only change the plan.

        Nothing of the plan starts while it is paused, not only nothing new:
        a story of Current sprint still waiting in the queue, not yet
        started, is held where it is, as a queued prompt being edited is
        held, as the @{QueueList} says, its card reading "Held for review",
        muted, and its lane waits on it; a story already running when the
        pause began runs on to its end, since stopping it would leave its
        work half done, and the bar says how many are still running. A
        chain's next step, as a story's steps are sent, is held the same
        way. Once the pause ends, by Resume or Approve, what was held goes
        on in its order, as though nothing had stopped it.

        The pause is plain to see: a bar across the top of the whole board,
        above every column, in the
        theme's warning colour, with a pause icon, reads "Paused for review",
        names the research it is waiting on, with a link that opens its
        findings, and holds two buttons, "Resume", which ends the pause, and
        "Approve and send sprint", which ends it and sends Next sprint at
        once. The Planning tab in the body shows a small pause icon beside
        its name, and the ribbon's Planning tab a warning dot, while it is
        paused. Pressing either button is the only way the pause ends;
        nothing the agent does, and no time passing, ends it. A second
        research while paused keeps the pause, naming the latest.

        The pause is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, with the research

I've added the wheel and trackpad rules to Planning's layout section, after the sentence about the board scrolling sideways. `piton check` and `piton build` both finished without errors.

The code should follow **[Planning.layout](.claude/reference/scope/planning/index.md#layout)**, in the paragraph that starts "Each column scrolls up and down on its own". What the spec now says:

- **Vertical wheel or two-finger swipe over a column, heading included:** scrolls only that column. It never moves the board sideways and never passes on to the board, even when the column is at its top or end or has nothing to scroll.
- **Shift+wheel or a sideways trackpad swipe anywhere on the board, over a column or not:** scrolls the board sideways while the columns are wider than the tab. While they fit, it does nothing.
- **Vertical wheel outside every column** (the padding, the 16-pixel gaps, the space beside the last column): scrolls the board sideways, as in Trello. I added one detail you didn't specify: scrolling down moves the board right, and up moves it left.
- **Diagonal trackpad swipe over a column:** the up-and-down part scrolls the column and the sideways part scrolls the board, both at once.
- **Side panel, pause bar and bulk bar:** scrolling over them never moves the board or a column. The side panel scrolls only itself, and the two bars scroll nothing.

The column and board scrollbars stay as [Scrollbar](.claude/reference/ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar) describes them.
